name: Long Put Condor
summary: Four puts at four ascending strikes - buy the lowest, sell the two middles, buy the highest - for a net debit; same flat-topped neutral payoff as a call condor, built in puts.

legs.strike_rule: strike B = A + W1 (body lower bound, below spot)
strike C: body upper bound, above spot
strike D = C + W1 (ITM put, outer widths equal)

max_profit: (W1 - net debit) x 100, between B and C
max_loss: net debit x 100, outside A and D
breakevens: A + net debit; D - net debit (per share)

greeks.delta: near zero with the body centered

when_to_use: Identical payoff to the call condor and the iron condor at the same strikes; useful when put strikes are better quoted or the put skew makes the debit cheaper. Range-bound view, IV rank >= 30.
entry_rules: Body centered within 0.25 x body width of spot
OI >= 500, spread <= 10% of mid on all four legs
Route only if cheaper than the equivalent iron condor and call condor
management_rules: Take profit at 50% of max profit
Loss stop at 50% of the debit
Close if spot leaves the A-D range
exit_rules: Force-close by 15:45 ET on expiration day, always
The upper short put (strike C) is ITM by construction - close the structure if its extrinsic < $0.10 or its delta <= -0.85
Short puts have no dividend-driven assignment, but deep ITM short puts are assigned when extrinsic vanishes, especially near expiry and around hard-to-borrow situations
Close immediately if either short strike is breached by more than 0.25 x W1
assignment_risk: The upper short put (C) is ITM for most of the trade's life; assignment delivers long shares (cash outlay of 100 x strike). No dividend trigger, but extrinsic-decay assignment is real.
liquidity_needs: All four legs OI >= 500; ITM put strikes often quoted wider - check before routing.
common_mistakes: Overpaying versus the equivalent iron condor; ignoring the ITM short put's assignment mechanics; body too narrow.
zero_dte_notes: Avoid - an ITM short put on expiration day will be assigned.
family: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
